newsitem.title: USA: Armco says demand, price outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Armco says demand, price outlook uncertain.

text.p: James Will, chairman and chief executive officer of Armco Inc, said the market outlook for demand and pricing of its products is uncertain.

He made the comment as Asarco reported a fourth quarter 1996 net income of $13.2 million or $0.08 a common share, against a net loss of $8.4 million or $0.12 a share for the comparable quarter in 1995.

While Armco has a strong order book for automotive chrome stainless in the first quarter, other products are not as strong, he said, adding he is concerned about price weakness as imports continue to depress volume and prices.
"We are encouraged by our improved performance in the fourth quarter," Will said, noting that the company's facility in Mansfield, Ohio, achieved profitability for the first time since its start-up.

"However, substantially higher imports had a serious impact on semi-finished and specialty sheet and strip, as transaction prices for these products deteriorated throughout the year, with that pricing weakness eventually spreading to other product lines."
He said equipment upgrades related to Armco's multi-year strategic facilities plan were completed in 1996 and are beginning to make a contribution to earnings.
Will said the company is focused on improving quality and manufacturing productivity and expects to achieve further cost reductions in 1997.
Armco is a leading domestic producer of specialty flat-rolled stainless, electrical and galvanized steels.
The company also produces snowplows and ice control products and standard pipe and tubular products.
